note.question: Can restrictions on ad targeting improve consumer welfare when a powerful platform adjusts ad rates and competitive advertisers respond through prices and advertising volume?
note.overview: A monopoly advertising platform sets ad rates anticipating a competitive product-market equilibrium in which advertisers choose advertising intensity and prices. The subgame-perfect analysis compares targetable no-privacy and nontargetable full-privacy regimes.

models.method: The authors formulate a two-stage platform leadership game with Butters-style informative advertising, derive equilibrium cumulative advertising distributions for given rates, optimize platform rates, and compare prices, ad volume, sales, platform revenue, customer-acquisition costs, and consumer surplus across privacy regimes and consumer-type configurations.

sources.quote: Under NP, there are potentially three target markets for each type of firm—type 1 consumers, type 2 consumers, all consumers—so the platform may quote six ad rates; under P, because the only target market is the set of all consumers, there are only two ad rates.21 The interaction between platform and advertisers is a two-stage game: the platform sets ad rates first; advertisers, taking those ad rates as given, then decide how many ads to buy and what product prices to advertise.

components.label: Information structure
components.explanation: Under no privacy, the platform observes consumer type and permits type-specific targeting and offers. Under full privacy, consumer type is unavailable, so every ad is randomly delivered across the whole market and product-price offers cannot be type-specific. Ads are informative, and a consumer knows only the products and prices in ads received. The platform anticipates the product-market advertising equilibrium induced by its ad rates.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: A privacy regime determines whether consumer types can be targeted. The platform first chooses ad rates by product type and feasible target market. Product firms then choose advertised prices and ad quantities; randomly exposed consumers select the offer producing the greatest positive surplus. The platform internalizes how its rates change both advertising intensity and advertised product-price distributions.

components.label: Subgame-perfect platform ad-rate and product-market advertising equilibrium
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Subgame-perfect platform ad-rate and product-market advertising equilibrium. The platform chooses ad rates first and product firms choose price-advertising distributions second. Definition 1 imposes platform revenue maximization and zero-positive-marginal-profit conditions, and the paper solves backward from product-market distributions to optimal rates in each privacy regime.
